content:
**Key visual observations:**

- **Affected part:** Stem base / soil line area
- **White cottony/fluffy mycelium:** Dense white fungal mat radiating outward from infected stem tissue — very prominent and characteristic
- **Small spherical structures (sclerotia):** Numerous small, round, yellowish-tan to cream-colored bodies scattered throughout the white mycelial mat — these match the "mustard seed"-sized sclerotia
- **Stem tissue:** Brown, degraded stem visible at the center
- The infection appears localized at the stem base

**Differential reasoning:**

- **Southern_Blight** — matches perfectly: white cottony mycelium radiating from stem base at/near soil line, with characteristic spherical sclerotia (here appearing light tan/cream-yellow, early stage). The description says "spherical sclerotia ranging from light tan to dark reddish-brown to black."
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** — also has white cotton-like mycelium, but its sclerotia are described as "hard, grayish-black, rice-grain sized" and embedded within the stem. The sclerotia here appear more numerous, spherical, and externally distributed on the mycelial mat — more consistent with Southern Blight (*Sclerotium rolfsii*).
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** — no fungal growth; bacterial streaming expected
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots** — would show black sporangia, not white cottony mats with separate sclerotia

The white fungal mats and numerous spherical sclerotia at the stem base are the definitive hallmarks of **Southern Blight**.

The sclerotia are round, mustard-seed sized, and distributed on the mycelial mat at the soil line, distinguishing this from Sclerotinia (which has larger, rice-grain-sized black sclerotia embedded within the stem)."}
